scene1_screen1.text: There are places in the galaxy that don’t exist on any official map. Zeta-9 is one of them. A red planet with no known history — until now.

scene1_screen2.text: The canyon is silent now, but an hour ago, the sky ripped open. Something ancient — a cosmic relic — plummeted through the atmosphere and rock, leaving a mile-wide crater pulsing faintly with blue light. The ground still shivers.

scene1_screen3.text: By the time Dr. Elizabeth Star touches down, she’s already scanning: seismic readings, energy signatures, gamma distortions. Everything in the data screams one impossible thing — this is real. The “Forgotten Star” wasn’t just a myth passed down through the Kaelari ruins. It landed.

scene1_screen4.text: She’s still tuning her scanner when a voice drips behind her, smug and maddeningly familiar.

scene1_screen6.text: She turns — and there he is. Leaning against his battered freighter like he’s posing for a holo-magazine titled Bad Decisions in Leather. Tousled hair, a scar on his temple she once kissed, and that same cocky grin that got her into trouble half a galaxy ago.

scene1_screen8.text: Former soldier. Now smuggler, a scavenger, a professional boundary-pusher. And once — briefly — her partner. Not just in fieldwork. In everything. She broke it off when the future started to matter.

scene1_screen10.text: Same as you. Following the signal. Only I got here first. As usual.

scene1_screen11.text: She’s about to reply when another ship descends — this one sleek, silver, and humming with silent threat. It bears the unmistakable sigil of House Auris. The ramp lowers before the dust settles.

scene1_screen12.text: A woman in matte white armor steps down. Braids tucked beneath her helm. Her movements are precise, regal. Her silence is louder than warnings. The air felt... hesitant. Like the planet itself was deciding whether to trust their footsteps.

scene1_screen13.text: This site is under the jurisdiction of House Auris. Unauthorized excavation is forbidden.

scene1_screen14.text: Commander Selene Auris. Noble blood. Head of the Preservation Accord. Known across the sectors not just as a political figure — but as the relentless hunter of the Kaelari relics. It is no secret: when ancient technology surfaces, she appears. And when she appears, entire expeditions vanish. She has the authority to shut down operations across any celestial body if she suspects a relic is involved — planet or star.

scene1_screen15.text: (tensing) I’m here under the Archaeological Fellowship. I have clearance to study planetary anomalies. Full spectrum.

scene1_screen16.text: Your credentials do not override the House claim. This planet was once Kaelari ground. The relic is Kaelari. That gives us total authority. And you know exactly what that means.

scene1_screen17.text: Elizabeth’s lips tighten. The Kaelari have been extinct for nine centuries, but their tech still pulses across forgotten systems. If the "Forgotten Star" truly is Kaelari… it would explain the impossible readings. The pulse. The crater that shouldn’t still be glowing.

scene1_screen18.text: (grinning) Look, I’m all for rules and righteous fury, but you’re not seriously telling me none of us get to peek at the shiny object that just crash-landed into reality?

scene1_screen19.text: You may observe. From the outer ring only. Cross the inner perimeter without permission, and the planet’s defense systems will react. They do not recognize friend from foe — not even Kaelari blood. And let me be clear — even I cannot pass unchallenged.

scene1_screen20.text: Elizabeth narrows her eyes. That’s new. If Selene is keeping them here… It’s because she can’t approach alone. The relic must be protected against her. Which means she needs them — at least for now.

scene1_screen21.text: Her scanner chirps, high-pitched. Localized tremors. Energy flares. The readings spike again. And something else: a ripple of destabilization. This artifact — whatever it is—is reacting. It’s waking up. And it’s not safe.

scene1_screen22.text: Elizabeth blinks at the data stream. Every star and planet not native to the relic’s origin appears vulnerable. Over time — days, maybe less — the artifact’s presence corrupts its environment. But on Kaelari soil? It harmonizes. She exhales. It’s him. The real one.

scene1_screen23.text: (sarcastically) So what — you’re letting us stay as long as we don’t breathe too loudly?

scene1_screen24.text: You have two days before this planet begins to collapse. The relic’s power is incompatible with Zeta-9’s core. Ever since she was stolen from my planet, she's been searching for a way back. Through pain. Through destruction. Your best — and only — chance to survive is working as one. And I will be watching every step.

opts.text: Agree reluctantly — focus on the mission
Team up — keep your companions close

scene1_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Fine. We do it your way. One team. Minimal cooperation. But I get access to the data. Full readings. No blackouts, no encrypted logs.

scene1_choice1_option1_screen3.text: Shawn quirks a brow but says nothing. Elizabeth already tunes him out — the mission comes first. It has to.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen1.text: This isn’t a tomb you can gatekeep, Selene. It’s a living relic. If you’re going to bury it in red tape and ancient law, I’ll go around you.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen2.text: You are welcome to try. But the moment you cross me, I activate the planetary lockdown protocol. That means only House vessels may exit. Everyone else — including you — dies with the star.

scene1_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Elizabeth freezes. That’s not posturing. That’s a nuclear option. And Selene’s hand is already near the console. She’ll have to outsmart her. Not out-title her.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Alright. We go together. You watch me. I watch the relic. And he — (gestures at Shawn) — keeps his hand to himself.

scene1_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Selene nods once, curt. The alliance is brittle. Full of silence, side-eyes, and unspoken threats. But it’ll hold. For now.

scene1_screen25.text: As the sun sinks below the horizon, the trio begins their slow approach to the crater. Beneath their feet, the planet groans. This isn’t just an artifact. It is destruction for some and salvation for others.

scene1_screen26.text: Elizabeth slowed her pace, glancing at the sky.

scene1_screen27.text: (thinking) It’s warm, but it doesn’t feel right. Like something’s been waiting too long.

scene2_screen1.text: The path beneath the crater spirals down into silence.

scene2_screen2.text: Alien glyphs glow faintly across the walls — not in steady light, but like breathing. Alive. Watching. They’re deeper now than any known Kaelari dig site. No drones, no comms. Just footsteps and the pulse of something ancient, waiting.

scene2_screen3.text: Selene moves ahead, holding a humming artifact, helping her in her search for a relic from her planet.. It resonates with the glyphs, unlocking a corridor like a whisper through stone. Ahead, the relic hovers — fragmented, delicate, impossibly powerful.

scene2_screen4.text: The legend said the Star would only awaken for those who care more for the galaxy than for themselves. Since the relic was torn from my planet's core, it has drifted, a severed heart without a home. On foreign soil, it destabilizes everything it touches. This is not revenge. It is a violation of the natural order. But for my planet, its absence is just as deadly. Without it, the planet withers, slowly but surely.

scene2_screen5.text: She looks at them both. Not with judgment — with certainty.

scene2_screen6.text: If we are here now, perhaps that is a sign.

scene2_screen7.text: Shawn can’t help it. The laugh escapes before he can stop it.

scene2_screen8.text: A cosmic relic chose us? One smuggler, one academic, and one knight with a really shiny sword? Sure. That checks out.

scene2_screen9.text: Selene doesn’t blink. But Elizabeth does — slow and tired.

scene2_screen10.text: (sardonically) You know who used to believe in signs? Earth. Now it's a footnote in a cautionary tale. Besides, we're not here for the Relic to reveal itself to us. I'm here to study it, Sean, we know why. Selene, you're here to return it to your planet, so I think we should just continue with our tasks.

scene2_screen11.text: There’s a flicker in her expression — not mockery, not dismissal. Just… Weight. Shawn watches her longer than he means to.

scene2_screen12.text: And then the relic pulses again — violently. Light explodes outward like a heartbeat, throwing heat and static into the air. The ground beneath them begins to shake and vibrate.

scene2_screen13.text: It’s reacting to emotional frequency. Move now or risk permanent collapse.

scene2_screen14.text: Elizabeth stumbles as the ground shifts. A crack opens near her feet.

scene2_screen15.text: Without thinking, Shawn grabs her — pulling her back from the edge.

scene2_screen16.text: Her breath catches against his chest, one hand pressed to the collar of his jacket. The silence between them feels… charged.

scene2_screen18.text: She’s still close. Her fingers still on him. The relic still pulsing. Something shifted — not just in the temple. In them.

scene2_choice1.text: How do you respond to the moment?

opts.text: Flirt — break the tension your way

scene2_choice1_option1_screen1.text: (quietly) You’re not used to falling, are you?

scene2_choice1_option1_screen2.text: She looks up, and for a second, there’s no sarcasm between them. Just breath and heartbeats and too many things left unsaid.

scene2_choice1_option1_screen4.text: He doesn’t move to let go. And she doesn’t ask him to.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen1.text: (grinning) If you wanted me to hold you, Professor… You could’ve just asked.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen2.text: Her eyes narrow, but her lips twitch like she’s fighting a smile.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen3.text: Keep talking like that, Way, and the relic won’t be the only thing that explodes.

scene2_choice1_option2_screen4.text: But she doesn’t step back. And he definitely doesn’t let go.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen1.text: (softly) I know this isn’t what you signed up for. But I’m glad I’m here. With you.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen2.text: She blinks. Her expression falters — just for a second. Then she exhales, slow and shaky.

scene2_choice1_option3_screen4.text: Neither of them says anything more. But the relic pulses brighter — as if it heard them.

scene2_screen19.text: They were separated from the relic by the shaking and the break, but they were lucky that all three of them remained close. They step away from each other. Just slightly. Just enough. But something lingers.

scene2_screen20.text: The closer they get to the artifact, the more the planet moves. This is no simple artifact. It's a test. And beating hearts seem to be part of the equation.

scene3_screen1.text: They walk in silence now. The rift separated them from the relic, and they´ll have to go through it to reach the relic from the other side. Its exact location was clear by its intense pulse.

scene3_screen2.text: Selene leads the group forward along the route of the supposed movement of the relic, but uncharted. Elizabeth follows, datapad in hand, noting readings that make little scientific sense. Shawn trails behind — blaster holstered, but watchful.

scene3_screen3.text: Then he hears it. A click, soft and sharp, from the rock wall above. Not the shifting of stone. Not a relic reaction. Something manmade.

scene3_screen6.text: Elizabeth lifts her head just as the first bolt strikes the wall beside her. The scorch mark is clean, military-grade. Not temple defense. Not ancient tech. Targeted. Controlled.

scene3_screen7.text: (firmly) These are mercenary rounds. Polished edge. Silent pattern. Someone hired professionals. And they’ve been tracking us.

scene3_screen8.text: Elizabeth stares at the blackened mark on the wall. Her stomach twists. Not a trap. A hunt.

scene3_screen9.text: The second shot comes faster — closer. Instinct takes over. Selene whirls, activating her blade. Shawn pulls Elizabeth behind an arching slab of Kaelari metal.

scene3_screen11.text: (low, shaken) I hope these aren't your friends.

scene3_screen12.text: They used to be. I didn’t know they’d follow me this far.

scene3_screen13.text: You always claimed they were just contacts. Just "necessary allies."

scene3_screen14.text: Yeah, well, turns out necessary turns toxic pretty fast.

scene3_screen15.text: That’s the thing, Shawn. You never saw the difference. Until it’s shooting at us.

scene3_screen16.text: Shawn looks at her. Her voice is steady, but her eyes are not. She isn’t scared for herself. She is afraid to find herself in a situation where she will have to choose herself again.

scene3_screen18.text: This is the relic's answer, follow me!

scene3_screen19.text: Minutes later — in a small side alcove. There was a rumble from another fissure and screams outside.

scene3_screen20.text: The mercs are now separated by a new crack, at least 7 hours away. They decide to camp here for the night and make plans. Fortunately, it was noticeable that the planet was starting to calm down.

scene3_screen21.text: Shawn went to check out the rift nearby and check if they were really safe for the night or not.

scene3_screen22.text: Selene, cleaning a cut on her arm, watches her for a moment.

scene3_screen23.text: I don't know if you know about this ability of people from my planet, but we, like the relic, feel people's emotions. You’re not just tired. You’re… grieving something. Something before.

scene3_screen24.text: Elizabeth tries to deflect. But Selene doesn’t press — she simply waits. And somehow, that’s worse. She feels the urge to share her experiences with Selene because they are troubling her greatly.

scene3_screen25.text: (quietly) Shawn and I… We worked together years ago. On Fornax. We made a good team — better than I ever expected. And when things started to shift between us, I... panicked. Besides, he was deaf to me when I asked him to leave his friends because I thought they were doing something wrong. I thought if I let it go further, I’d lose focus. Become someone’s other half instead of myself.

scene3_screen26.text: So you chose to walk away.

scene3_screen27.text: I chose control. I told myself it was for science. But I think I was just afraid he’d be the one thing I couldn’t catalogue or predict.

scene3_screen28.text: Selene nods once, thoughtful. Then gestures to her broken comm unit.

scene3_screen29.text: The uplink’s damaged. I’ll try to reestablish contact from the outer ridge. You’ll be safe here for now. Use the time wisely.

scene3_screen31.text: You're leaving us alone on purpose.

scene3_screen32.text: (softly) I believe the relic brought all three of us here for a reason. But I also believe in second chances. For more than just relics.

scene3_screen33.text: Left alone, Elizabeth decided to make a little imitation of an overnight stay.

scene3_screen34.text: After a while, Shawn returned. Elizabeth stands, brushing dust from her knees. She finds Shawn leaning against a pillar, arms crossed — not cocky now. Just… present.

scene3_screen35.text: I think we have something to discuss. About us.

scene3_screen37.text: A small part. Or a large part. Who knows.

scene3_screen39.text: I meant what I said. I was scared.

scene3_screen40.text: You didn’t owe me anything. You owe yourself a little mercy, though.

opts.text: Let him speak — give him space
Flirt — keep it light, but real

scene3_choice1_option1_screen1.text: I don’t want to rewrite the past. But maybe we can start something new. Smarter. Slower. Real.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen2.text: I want you to know that I have no more ties to the swindlers. I listened to you, even though it was later. My subsequent searches were not for the relics, but to find you.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen3.text: If that´s true, perhaps we can build something new together.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen4.text: He steps toward her — just enough. She closes the space. The kiss is quiet. Measured. Earned.

scene3_choice1_option1_screen6.text: When they pull apart, the room feels warmer.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen1.text: If you have something to say, say it.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen2.text: I was angry at first. Then I got it. You were building a future. I was... running from mine. I was afraid to break ties with the criminal world. Now it's over.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen3.text: She places a hand on his chest, above the beat she knows too well.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen4.text: So maybe this time we walk toward it. Together.

scene3_choice1_option2_screen5.text: They don’t kiss. Not yet. But his fingers curl around hers, and it’s enough.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen1.text: You know, back on Fornax, I made a list of all the reasons you’d be bad for me.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen3.text: Too charming. Too chaotic. Too distracting.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen4.text: And yet here we are. By the way, I broke up with my accomplices. You don't have anything to worry about anymore.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen6.text: I might be ready to cross-check my data.

scene3_choice1_option3_screen7.text: He smiles — and this time, so does she.

scene3_screen42.text: The moment’s cut short by footsteps. Selene steps into the light, dusted with sand, holding the flickering uplink unit.

scene3_screen43.text: Signal’s restored. I sent a low-pulse ping to orbit. If we don’t find the relic before the star’s destruction, they can still pull us out. But we’d hate to miss it.

scene3_screen44.text: She pauses, seeing how close they’re standing. A brow lifts — the only reaction.

scene3_screen45.text: I’ll give you a moment. Or pretend I didn’t see it. Your call.

scene3_screen46.text: Elizabeth straightens, trying (badly) to look composed. Shawn just laughs, entirely unapologetic.

scene3_screen47.text: Elizabeth and Shawn seemed to no longer feel the tension that had been there since their breakup. Outside, the relic pulses again. Slower. Steadier. Like it feels the tension between survival… and something else. Like it approves.

scene4_screen1.text: The air smells faintly of dust and ozone. Somewhere, the relic pulses gently — not warning, not reacting. Just breathing.

scene4_screen2.text: For once, there is no gunfire, no tremors. Just rock, and silence, and a strange sense of stillness.

scene4_screen3.text: Elizabeth unpacks a small cloth roll from her satchel and reveals dried fruit, protein strips, and something that might be chocolate. A surprise, even to Shawn.

scene4_screen4.text: You packed snacks for an apocalypse?

scene4_screen5.text: Academic rule number one: Never excavate on an empty stomach.

scene4_screen6.text: She passes pieces around. Even Selene accepts hers, albeit wordlessly. They sit in a soft triangle of light. The silence feels thicker than the dust around them — but eventually, it breaks.

scene4_screen7.text: Alright. We’re alive. We’re sitting still. That’s rare. So tell me — off the record, no noble speeches — Why the hell are we really doing this?

scene4_screen8.text: (staring into the fire) I used to think knowledge was enough. That if I catalogued enough ruins, published enough papers, I’d matter. I grew up reading about the stars, but it was my brother who actually got to chase them. When he died on an expedition, I promised myself I’d never just read again. I’d be the one discovering.

scene4_screen9.text: (sincerely) So you came looking for meaning?

scene4_screen10.text: I came looking for something that wouldn't disappear.

scene4_screen11.text: That is not the same as believing in purpose.

scene4_screen12.text: Maybe not. But it’s enough to keep walking. Sometimes that’s all we get.

scene4_screen13.text: I was raised in orbit stations. After the Earth was destroyed by the Kaelar relic. I never saw the real sky until I was twelve. Spent most of my life stealing from people who deserved it — and a few who didn’t. Once, I couldn't choose between what I knew and loved. Then I heard about the relic and thought that, wherever it was, I would see the one thing I had lost again.

scene4_screen14.text: His eyes flick briefly to Elizabeth. She doesn’t look away this time.

scene4_screen15.text: You speak of loss. Of ghosts. But this relic… it is not a symbol. It was stolen. Ripped from my planet’s heart. And since then — It has killed everything it touches. Not because it wants to. Because it doesn’t belong.

scene4_screen17.text: Her voice doesn't rise. But the weight in it silences the air around them.

scene4_screen18.text: Without it, my planet decays — cell by cell, storm by storm. But on other worlds… the relic corrupts. Burns. Destroys. Not vengeance. Just imbalance. I’m here because my people have twenty years left. Maybe less.

scene4_screen19.text: She stands slowly, adjusting the clasp on her armor.

scene4_screen20.text: I’ll take first watch. Enjoy your rest.

scene4_screen21.text: And without waiting for an answer, she disappears into the violet-tinted darkness of the passage.

scene4_screen22.text: After a while… Shawn and Elizabeth are alone. The fire crackles low. Elizabeth stretches her legs out, gaze following the shadows where Selene vanished.

scene4_screen23.text: She makes me feel... inadequate. She has a mission to save her people, and you and I are just adventure seekers. And I want to help her.

scene4_screen24.text: Because you understand her. Even if she doesn’t see it.

scene4_screen25.text: Elizabeth turns toward him, brows lifted.

scene4_screen28.text: They sit close now. The warmth is not just from the fire. Elizabeth looks at him, really looks, and sees not the smuggler, not the flirt, but the man who, as it turned out, went on a trip to see her again. They missed each other, their feelings were clearly mutual they asked nothing for it. Who stayed.

scene4_choice1.text: How do you respond to this moment?

opts.text: Open heart — tell her how you feel
Play it light — but still true

scene4_choice1_option1_screen1.text: You don’t have to explain. You just have to know — I’m here. Not chasing. Not running. Just… here.

scene4_choice1_option1_screen2.text: He lifts her hand gently. His thumb brushes over her knuckles. No pressure. No assumption. Just care.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen1.text: I’ve been a dozen things in my life. But with you… I want to be something better.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen2.text: His voice is low, rough around the edges.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen3.text: She leans her forehead against his.

scene4_choice1_option2_screen5.text: They kiss. They breathe — together — and that’s enough.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen1.text: Just for the record, you’re not inadequate. You’re terrifyingly brilliant. And insanely good at packing snacks.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen2.text: She lets out a breathy laugh, eyes softening.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen3.text: You’re not so bad yourself. For a walking court-martial.

scene4_choice1_option3_screen4.text: Their shoulders brush. Their smiles stay. The rest can wait.

scene4_screen30.text: They sit like that for a while, watching the fire flicker and fade.

scene4_screen31.text: And when Elizabeth finally speaks again, it’s not to him, not exactly.

scene4_screen32.text: Maybe there is something to this "fate" thing after all.

scene4_screen33.text: She closes her eyes. And the relic stirs again — faint, distant — like it’s listening.

scene5_screen1.text: Shawn is already awake when he sees Selene approaching the camp.

scene5_screen2.text: Nice to see your kind doesn’t need much sleep.

scene5_screen3.text: That’s one downside of Earthborns. That, and claiming what never belonged to them.

scene5_screen4.text: Well, I apologize on behalf of my ancestors.

scene5_screen5.text: He raised his hands in a mock-surrender. Selene rolled her eyes slightly.

scene5_screen6.text: You really don’t let anyone oversleep, do you?

scene5_screen7.text: There’ll be time for rest—if we find the relic. Speaking of which, I found what may be a passage leading to it during my patrol. But I’ll need your help retrieving it.

scene5_screen9.text: They walked for nearly three hours. Their thoughts began to slip—subtle, as if from oxygen deprivation. None of them wanted to admit weakness, yet something about the relic’s proximity was affecting them all.

scene5_screen10.text: I felt it too. It’s the relic’s influence. When we get closer, you’ll likely be asked to make a moral choice— one that will charge the relic and allow us to dislodge it. It doesn’t ask me. I’m part of its lineage. But you… It seems to be watching you.

scene5_screen11.text: They neared the impact site. Now, it’s only a matter of answering the fate that brought the three of them together.

scene5_screen12.text: The relic lies in the center of the stone. Its glow is unmistakable— as if it’s been waiting not for someone strong, but someone willing to understand.

scene5_screen13.text: They stand in silence before the relic. The glowing emerald pulses slowly—its light somehow… aware. Selene steps closer but stops, lowering her gaze.

scene5_screen14.text: It won’t respond to me. I tried to contact her from afar, but she's silent. Even if I came here alone, I wouldn't be able to take her; she would destroy my ship, I can feel it. It still remembers being stolen from Earth. It doesn't forgive.

scene5_screen15.text: That… doesn’t make sense. You’re one of its people.

scene5_screen16.text: And still, it sees me as the child of a failing empire. But I believe… maybe together, we can reach it. I guess the relic sees us differently than we see each other.  Three of us. One to offer forgiveness. One to ask for it. One to promise protection.

scene5_screen17.text: She turns to Elizabeth—her expression unexpectedly soft.

scene5_screen18.text: Elizabeth. You forgave him… didn’t you? The relic will no longer be troubled by power or lineage alone. There must be harmony between the one who forgives, the one who repents, and the one who promises never to let this happen again.

scene5_screen19.text: (quietly) He left the smuggling life. For me, for this mission. He made the step. I followed with mine.

scene5_screen20.text: Shawn shifts slightly, uneasy but proud. Selene nods, then looks at him.

scene5_screen21.text: And you, Shawn… are you ready to speak for all Earthborns who failed before you?

scene5_screen22.text: If that’s what it takes to make it right—I will. We took what wasn’t ours. Maybe it’s time we finally returned something.

scene5_screen23.text: The relic glows brighter as they step closer. Selene kneels first, placing her hand near the emerald. Elizabeth and Shawn exchange a look—one filled with emotion, history, and something new. They kneel.

scene5_screen24.text: The emerald flares—waves of light sweep over them. For a moment, the world fades. Only connection remains. The relic pulses, sensing intention. All eyes are on Elizabeth. She has the first word.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen1.text: Maybe I was wrong to think I could do this alone. Maybe... maybe it was never about the data. (She turns to Shawn, voice softer) You already made your choice. Maybe it’s time I made mine.

scene5_choice1_option1_screen2.text: She takes his hand. No grand declaration — just trust. Just this moment. The relic brightens, just slightly. Selene watches in silence, something like understanding in her eyes.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen1.text: We’re not here to play out some cosmic love story. I’m here for the relic. For the knowledge. (She steps back) Let’s finish what we started.

scene5_choice1_option2_screen2.text: Shawn nods, a flicker of disappointment crossing his face. The relic dims, but does not resist. Selene tightens her grip on her staff — they’ll have to work harder.

scene5_screen25.text: The relic now turns its attention to him. Not with judgment — but expectation.

scene5_choice2.text: What do you say as a representative of Earth’s legacy?

scene5_choice2_option1_screen1.text: We stole what wasn’t ours. Again and again. I can’t change that. But I can stand here and say it was wrong. And maybe (pauses) Maybe that means something.

scene5_choice2_option1_screen2.text: The relic responds — a faint warmth rising through the crater. Selene lowers her gaze. Not forgiveness. But the beginning of it.

scene5_choice2_option2_screen1.text: You want atonement? That’s for ghosts. But I can offer something better: a promise. (as he steps forward) Let me help guard it. Guard you. If I’m going to carry Earth’s sins, let me do it on the right side.

scene5_choice2_option2_screen2.text: Selene meets his eyes. She sees the rogue, the smuggler... and the man trying to change. The relic hums, steady and alive.

scene5_screen26.text: The emerald settles—its light is calm. Selene slowly stands, her posture straighter than before.

scene5_screen27.text: The relic… accepts us. And it’s ready to return home.

scene5_screen28.text: So are we going to your world?

scene5_screen29.text: (smiling for the first time) You’ve both earned a place there. Zeta will welcome you—as it once welcomed the stars.

scene5_screen30.text: They walk away from the crater together. No longer strangers, no longer alone.

scene6_screen1.text: Selene holds the relic aloft before her people — its light now steady and warm. The people feel the return of the relic. They are proud of Selene, who was able to return it to the planet and save them.

scene6_screen2.text: Behind her, stand Shawn and Elizabeth — no longer just adventurers. But honored guests. Partners in peace.

scene6_screen3.text: The once-broken terrain now hums with new life — small shoots sprouting from dust, the air warmer, gentler. The relic works fast. But not alone.

scene6_screen4.text: People of Kaelari… We honor not just the relic today, but those who returned it. These two— (points to Elizabeth and Shawn) — are now honored citizens of our world.

scene6_screen5.text: They didn’t come to save us. And yet… they did. Not through power. Through trust, courage… and a little stubborn Earth grit.

scene6_screen6.text: The crowd erupts in applause. Not formal. Not polite. Loud. Emotional. Real.

scene6_screen7.text: (smiling at Shawn) I’m glad you followed the relic… But I’m even gladder you were really chasing me.

scene6_screen8.text: (grinning) And I’m glad you forgave me. Next time, I say we chase something with fewer booby traps.

scene6_screen10.text: (teasing) And I’m just glad fate dropped two Earthlings into my planetary crisis. Worked out alright, didn’t it?

scene6_screen11.text: They laugh. The relic glows stronger, like it, too, approves. The stars begin to rise over the amphitheater. Peace, for once, feels earned.

scene6_screen12.text: And as night wraps the planet in its quiet brilliance, only one question remains: Will they journey together again? That… is a tale for another time.
